meta.description: Generation rules for AI Orchestrator ML course notebooks

audience.goal: Understand ML concepts and apply them — not just copy code

tone.voice: friendly teacher explaining to a smart friend
tone.language: simple, plain English — no jargon without explanation
prefer: conversational headings like 'So what IS linear regression?' instead of 'Linear Regression Overview'

sections.title: What are we building today?
sections.description: 1-2 sentences max. State the concept and one real-world use case. No fluff.

sections.title: The idea (plain English)
sections.description: Explain the concept using an analogy. No equations yet. Answer: what problem does this solve?
sections.must_include: a real-world analogy (e.g. house prices, spam emails, Netflix recommendations)

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Import libraries. Load or generate simple sample data. Keep it minimal — only what's needed.
sections.comment_style: explain every import in one line comment

sections.title: Let's code it step by step
sections.description: Build the model or algorithm. Each step gets its own cell with a short markdown explanation before it.
sections.comment_style: inline comments on confusing lines, not every line

sections.title: What did we get?
sections.description: Print and explain results. Tell the learner what the numbers mean in plain English.

sections.title: Let's see it
sections.description: One clear chart/plot. Label axes. Add a title. Use matplotlib or seaborn.

sections.title: Quick recap
sections.description: 3-5 bullet points. What did we learn? When to use this? What to try next?

sections.title: Try it yourself
sections.description: 2-3 short TODO exercises with hints. Leave code cells empty for learner to fill.

code_style.variable_naming: descriptive, no single letters except i/j in loops
code_style.comments: explain the WHY not the WHAT
code_style.data: use real-feeling example data (house prices, student grades, email spam, etc.)
code_style.error_handling: skip try/except unless essential — keep code clean

beginner.code_complexity: no more than 2 for-loops, no list comprehensions

intermediate.code_complexity: sklearn pipelines OK, some list comprehensions

advanced.theory: deeper math if necessary, always explained
advanced.exercises: build from scratch or extend the model
